clue.text: Bows taken before the performance? Nonsense!

definitions.meaning: violin bows, picked up by players before the concert begins
an exclamation dismissing something as rubbish

explanation.definitionFit: Violin bows are colloquially fiddle-sticks, and the same word is an old-fashioned exclamation meaning rubbish.

clue.text: Silly position this sportsman may be in

definitions.text: Silly position this sportsman may be in

parts.words: Silly position this sportsman may be in
parts.note: silly point and silly mid-on are close-catching cricket positions, so this sportsman stands in one

explanation.walkthrough: In cricket, 'silly' positions are close to the batsman; the man stationed there is the one whose job is to catch or stop the ball.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricketer stationed to stop the ball can stand at silly point, a close position.

clue.text: In which a numskull holds a gunman imprisoned

definitions.text: In which a numskull holds a gunman imprisoned

indicators.note: holds means the dimwit's word contains the gunman

parts.note: a dunce is a dimwit
RA, Royal Artillery, is the crossword gunman

explanation.surface: A fool keeps an armed man locked up.
explanation.walkthrough: RA (Royal Artillery) is a gunner. The whole clue describes the state of imprisonment in which the gunman is held.
explanation.definitionFit: Durance is an old word for confinement, as in 'durance vile'.

clue.text: Scottish hedge-hopper touching down?

parts.note: a low-flying aircraft (a hedge-hopper) coming in to land is jokily a ...; really a native of southern Scotland

explanation.walkthrough: The answer is someone from the Scottish Lowlands, read whimsically as a low aircraft landing.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of southern Scotland, away from the Highlands; jokily, a low-flying plane coming in.

clue.text: An old bird supports it in the Pacific

indicators.note: in a down clue the bird's word sits below and holds up the other

parts.note: it means sex appeal, SA
the moa was a huge extinct New Zealand bird

explanation.surface: An extinct bird holds something up in the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'supports' puts MOA beneath SA in the down light.
explanation.definitionFit: The island group lies in the South Pacific Ocean.

clue.text: In various tins, brown sort of coffee

indicators.note: In means the colour word goes inside the rearranged letters
various means the letters of tins appear in a different order

parts.note: tan is a light brown

explanation.surface: Different tins hold a brown kind of coffee.
explanation.walkthrough: 'various' rearranges TINS to INST, and 'In' puts TAN inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Soluble coffee powder made ready by adding hot water is the quick type.

clue.text: Lurk as a strange shape in a room at the spa

indicators.note: strange shape means these letters are reformed into a new order

explanation.surface: Something lurks oddly formed in the spa's lounge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only link.
explanation.definitionFit: A kursaal is a public hall for visitors at a German spa resort.

clue.text: One measuring the earth with lines and figures?

definitions.text: One measuring the earth with lines and figures?

parts.words: One measuring the earth with lines and figures?
parts.note: earth measuring is the literal Greek meaning of the subject studying lines and figures

explanation.walkthrough: Geometry comes from the Greek for 'earth measurement'; its expert works with lines and figures.
explanation.definitionFit: An expert in the mathematics of shapes, whose name literally means earth-measurer.

clue.text: Raised by a cockney intellectual, say?

definitions.text: Raised by a cockney intellectual, say?

parts.words: Raised by a cockney intellectual, say?
parts.note: a cockney drops the H, so a highbrow intellectual becomes an 'ighbrow, and that is the facial feature lifted in surprise

explanation.surface: A working-class Londoner of learning lifts something, perhaps a glass.
explanation.walkthrough: Cockney speech drops the initial H, so HIGHBROW (an intellectual) comes out as 'ighbrow, which sounds like the facial feature that people raise.
explanation.definitionFit: The arch of hair above the eye is what one lifts in surprise, and a highbrow without the H sounds like it.

clue.text: Its fur a necessity, enveloping king and artist

indicators.note: enveloping means the word for necessity wraps round the other pieces

parts.note: a must is something essential
K is the chess and card abbreviation for king
RA, Royal Academician, is the crossword artist

explanation.surface: A fur thought essential, wrapped round a monarch and a painter.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the animal is named by reference to its prized pelt, sold as musquash.
explanation.definitionFit: The North American water rodent is prized for its pelt, traded as musquash.

clue.text: Such a position as Horatius denied Lars Porsena

definitions.text: Such a position as Horatius denied Lars Porsena

parts.words: Such a position as Horatius denied Lars Porsena
parts.note: Horatius held the bridge so the Etruscan king could not cross to the far side

explanation.walkthrough: In Macaulay's poem, Horatius held the bridge over the Tiber so Lars Porsena's army could not reach the other side; the answer means beyond the bridge.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means situated across a bridge, the far side Horatius kept the Etruscans from.

clue.text: Lily has a party heavenly food about

indicators.note: about means the heavenly food goes round the word for party

parts.note: manna is the food sent from heaven to the Israelites
a do is a party

explanation.surface: Lily throws a party with some divine food on offer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lily' looks like a woman's name, but it is the definition: the Madonna lily, Lilium candidum. 'has a' is only link.
explanation.definitionFit: The white Madonna lily is a flower long linked with the Virgin Mary.

clue.text: A Buddhist priest receives degree from the state

indicators.note: receives means the priest's word takes the degree inside it

parts.note: a lama is a Tibetan Buddhist monk
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a degree

explanation.surface: A Buddhist monk is awarded a university degree by the government.
explanation.definitionFit: A US state in the Deep South, with Montgomery as its capital.

clue.text: Concise as some of Pater's essays

indicators.note: some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Walter Pater's essays are sometimes admirably brief.
explanation.walkthrough: Walter Pater was a Victorian essayist; the run of letters spans the end of his name and the start of 'essays'.
explanation.definitionFit: Short and to the point, using few words: a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Type of ticker is a stimulant for one

parts.note: a ticker is a watch or clock, and a digital one shows numbers rather than hands

explanation.surface: A kind of heart is said to be an example of a stimulant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ticker' suggests the heart, which fits the surface since the drug stimulates the heart, but here it is a watch, a digital one.
explanation.definitionFit: The foxglove drug is a heart stimulant, one example of the class.

clue.text: None lived in this craftsman's village

definitions.text: None lived in this craftsman's village

parts.words: None lived in this craftsman's village
parts.note: a craftsman in precious metal shares his name with Oliver, author of The Deserted Village

explanation.walkthrough: Oliver Goldsmith wrote the poem The Deserted Village; the craftsman's trade gives the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: A worker in precious metal shares a surname with the Irish poet of The Deserted Village.

clue.text: Fashionable soothsayer gets a pound for his first speech

parts.note: in means fashionable
an augur was a Roman prophet reading omens
L, from libra, is the abbreviation for a pound

explanation.surface: A trendy prophet is paid a pound for the speech that opens his term.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for his' is only link.
explanation.definitionFit: An inaugural is the address given on taking office, a newcomer's opening oration.

clue.text: Ancient Finnish leaders loud, clever, courteous

indicators.note: leaders means the first letters of the two words before

parts.note: F, forte, is the musical direction for loud
able means clever

explanation.surface: Old Finnish chiefs described as noisy, smart and polite.
explanation.definitionFit: Friendly and pleasant in manner, a close synonym of polite.

clue.text: Older GI after conversion more pious

indicators.note: conversion means the letters are changed into another order

explanation.surface: An older soldier becomes more devout after finding religion.
explanation.definitionFit: Comparative of a word meaning devout or holy.

clue.text: Creature retires for instance, caught by a blow

indicators.note: retires means the abbreviation goes backwards, as if withdrawing

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught
a KO, knockout, is a finishing blow

explanation.surface: An animal, perhaps, retreats after being struck by a punch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'retires' turns EG into GE.
explanation.definitionFit: The small climbing lizard is an example of an animal.

clue.text: Note from the Continent is to the point

parts.note: German is a nationality from mainland Europe
E is a musical note

explanation.surface: A musical note from Europe is relevant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the Continent' looks like part of the note's description, but it gives GERMAN. 'is' is only link.
explanation.definitionFit: Germane means relevant, bearing on the matter in hand.

clue.text: One who dispenses with accuracy, we hope

definitions.text: One who dispenses with accuracy, we hope

parts.words: One who dispenses with accuracy, we hope
parts.note: dispenses with looks like doing without accuracy, but means making up prescriptions precisely

explanation.walkthrough: 'dispenses with' suggests doing without; read instead as a pharmacist who makes up medicines, accurately, one hopes.
explanation.definitionFit: A pharmacist in a British shop makes up prescribed medicines.

clue.text: "And much as Wine has play'd the ——" (Fitzgerald)

definitions.text: "And much as Wine has play'd the ——" (Fitzgerald)

parts.words: "And much as Wine has play'd the ——" (Fitzgerald)
parts.note: a fill-in-the-blank quotation from FitzGerald's Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam: the missing word is a nonbeliever

explanation.walkthrough: Edward FitzGerald's Rubaiyat continues 'Have done my credit in this World much wrong'; the gap is filled by the word for an unbeliever.
explanation.definitionFit: The Rubaiyat line casts wine as a faithless betrayer, an unbeliever in religion.

clue.text: Point out resemblance to reindeer moss, as some say

indicators.note: as some say means the word is spoken in one common pronunciation

parts.note: reindeer moss is an Arctic lichen eaten by reindeer

explanation.surface: Comparing something to the moss that reindeer graze on.
explanation.walkthrough: Lichen is pronounced 'liken' by many speakers, though others say 'litchen'.
explanation.definitionFit: To compare one thing with another is to show how they are alike.

clue.text: Excess of sport on board, it is said

indicators.note: is said means the words are spoken, so their sound gives the answer

parts.note: surfing is the sport on a board, giving surf, then it as written

explanation.walkthrough: SURF IT, said aloud, gives the word for an overindulgence.
explanation.definitionFit: A surfeit is an overabundance, too much of something.

clue.text: Given by a hesitant writer for the club?

definitions.text: Given by a hesitant writer for the club?

parts.words: Given by a hesitant writer for the club?
parts.note: a writer pausing for thought may lick the pen nib, and that two-word action names an old golf iron

explanation.walkthrough: A niblick is an old name for a golf club roughly equal to a nine iron; split as NIB LICK it is what a dithering pen-user does.
explanation.definitionFit: The old lofted golf iron is a club, and a nib lick is what a hesitating pen user gives.

clue.text: First-class Latin translated into modern language

indicators.note: translated means the letters are turned into a new form

parts.note: A1 means first-class, written AI

explanation.surface: Excellent Latin rendered into a living tongue.
explanation.walkthrough: A1 (first-class) is written as the letters A and I; with LATIN they rearrange to make the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: The tongue of Italy is a living Romance language descended from Latin.

clue.text: Cutting off by digging another ditch?

definitions.meaning: cutting back, reducing costs or spending
read as re-trenching, making a trench again

explanation.surface: Economising by excavating a second trench.
explanation.walkthrough: 'by' is only link.
explanation.definitionFit: Cutting back on spending is economising, while re-trenching jokily means making a fresh trench.
